questions.q: What lesson does Jeff draw from the night his infant son would not go back to sleep?
a: Letting go of expectations let him notice a special moment
A strict bedtime routine makes babies calmer
Parents should trade nights to avoid exhaustion
Babies learn new words best late at night
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes how giving up on sleep led him to play with his son and hear new words.

questions.q: What does the summary say happens when plans go off-track?
a: That is often when real life happens
It is a sign the original plan was wrong
It should be corrected as quickly as possible
It usually makes the outcome much worse
questions.why: Lesson 1 says life happens right when things go wrong or off-track, if you stop and give up control.

questions.q: What changed Jeff's view of the dull cross-country train ride?
a: A fellow passenger's joy at going home
The scenery suddenly becoming dramatic
A book he found to pass the time
A decision to get off at the next stop
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes a florist who called the landscape beautiful and spoke of going home.

questions.q: What did the florist on the train teach Jeff?
a: The people we love can make any landscape beautiful
Travel is the best way to learn about yourself
Strangers rarely want to talk on long trips
Home is usually less interesting than new places
questions.why: Lesson 2 says thinking of the people who matter can turn a barren winter landscape into beautiful scenery.

questions.q: What does the summary advise about big life events like weddings?
a: Celebrate them fully when they happen
Plan them carefully years in advance
Treat them as ordinary days to avoid disappointment
Focus on them instead of everyday moments
questions.why: Lesson 3 says big moments are rare, so give them attention and be grateful when they occur.
